outcome: composite neonatal outcome (umbilical artery pH < 7.1, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and 5-min Apgar score < 7)
cohort: The study included nulliparous women with a singleton gestation who underwent term vaginal delivery or vacuum-assisted delivery.
finding: Mediolateral episiotomy showed no significant protective effect against obstetric anal sphincter injuries in vaginal deliveries, but demonstrated a possible protective benefit in vacuum-assisted deliveries, particularly in cases of prolonged second stages of labor.
mod_finding: While mediolateral episiotomy showed no significant protective effect on obstetric anal sphincter injuries in spontaneous vaginal deliveries, it demonstrated a possible benefit in vacuum-assisted deliveries, especially with a prolonged second stage of labor.
